# A two-way prop the caller leaves unbound is state of the instance, run on
# every target a test can execute on.
#
# testdata/unbound_prop_state.txtar is the code; this is the answer. The
# checkbox nobody binds keeps what the host reports, a read of `box.checked`
# reads that cell, and a one-way value is where the cell starts rather than a
# value the widget is held to. A compiled target's test reads a component's
# state and not a widget's, so the handler writes what the read answered into
# `seen`; the handler runs after the host's report has written the cell, as a
# binding's write-back runs before its handler.
#
# The flips alternate from the state each control is in, because bubbletea's
# key press and android's click flip the control whatever the test passed.
#
# refs.sngl reads the cells off the handles, which only the interpreter's test
# surface can do: through the node, in the text beside it, and per row of a
# loop, each row's cell its own.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=none refs.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --opt testRunner=robolectric app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

[!gtk4] stop 'gtk4 needs its development libraries to build'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

component main node {
    var seen = "none"
    vbox {
        checkbox #box(label="alone", @change { seen = "box {box.checked}" })
        checkbox #start(checked=true, label="starts on", @change { seen = "start {start.checked}" })
    }
}

func testUnboundKeepsWhatTheHostReports(t Test, c main) {
    c.box.change(true)
    t.assert(c.seen == "box true")
    c.box.change(false)
    t.assert(c.seen == "box false")
}

func testOneWayValueIsWhereItStarts(t Test, c main) {
    c.start.change(false)
    t.assert(c.seen == "start false")
    c.start.change(true)
    t.assert(c.seen == "start true")
}

window {
    main
}
-- refs.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

component main node {
    var items = ["a", "b"]
    vbox {
        checkbox #box(label="alone")
        text #shown(value=box.checked ? "on" : "off")
        checkbox #start(checked=true, label="starts on")
        for var it = items {
            checkbox #row(label=it)
        }
    }
}

func testReadOffTheHandle(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.box.checked == false)
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "off")
    c.box.change(true)
    t.assert(c.box.checked == true)
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "on")
    t.assert(c.start.checked == true)
    c.start.change(false)
    t.assert(c.start.checked == false)
}

func testEachRowKeepsItsOwn(t Test, c main) {
    c.row[1].change(true)
    t.assert(c.row[0].checked == false)
    t.assert(c.row[1].checked == true)
}

window {
    main
}
